newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador to study oil deals with Chile's ENAP.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador to study oil deals with Chile's ENAP.

text.p: A delegation from Chile's national oil company ENAP will arrive in Ecuador next week to study possible investments, a Chilean diplomat said Friday.

"We've had a favorable meeting with (Ecuadorean Energy) Minister Raul Baca and on Tuesday we will receive an ENAP mission to hold meetings with local authorities," embassy economic advisor Hernan Mena told Reuters.
Two years ago ENAP and other Chilean companies, including the oil firm COPEC, set up the holding company Sipetrol Chile and signed a cooperation agreement with Ecuador's state-run Petroecuador.
"Under this cooperation agreement we will hold several rounds of talks aimed at signing a bilateral government agreement to purchase crude oil," Mena said.
"Eventually we will study the renewal of sales of Chilean diesel and airplane fuel to Ecuador," he added.
Mena said next week's meetings would also focus on future expansion plans for Petroecuador, such as the extension of the Trans-Ecuadorean pipleline and new storage facilities in the Balao district.
Ecuador produces some 390,000 daily barrels of crude, of which 340,000 are carried by the Trans-Ecuadorean pipeline and the rest by the Trans-Andean pipeline.
Oil is Ecuador's main source of income.
